rv.q: But as much as “Kenrex” can feel like a punch, you have to wonder who or what the target is.
Holden and Stambollouian are authoritatively present, and that’s plenty.
Stambollouian delivers a non-stop spectacle with breathtaking theatrical force.
With stunning design and a phenomenal solo performance by Holden, Kenrex expertly toes delicate balances between entertainment and tragedy, and community and individual.
“Kenrex” ultimately delivers because Holden’s portrayal of the title character is a strong, frightening piece of work.
Despite its shortcomings, “Kenrex” offers a vivid and engaging study of the subject.
Holden’s rocking performance does tend to put the spotlight more on him than the people of Skidmore.
While recognizing how a great deal of ingenuity and skill goes into making Kenrex an impressive achievement of sorts, I must admit to not much liking the show.
Kenrex is brave and bravura work, a showcase for Holden's virtuosity as both a writer and performer.
Returning to KENREX in this new space does not simply revisit a story already told.
This isn’t just good theater—it’s essential, electrifying storytelling.
Holden, who won two Olivier Awards including Best Actor, does not simply perform these roles—he inhabits them.

cn.t: Jack Holden's tour-de-force solo performance electrifies critics in this true-crime thriller, though some question the material's purpose beyond showcasing his impressive ability to embody 35 characters.

vr.q: Shows like this don't come around all that often. This is unique and exciting and engaging and compelling... Take people to go and see this who don't think they like theater and convert them for life.
